title: The constructed integral, rational and sheafified-colimit lines are locally free of rank one over their respective pulled-back condensed coefficient r
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $X$ such that $\ell$ is invertible in every residue field, and a finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. Use the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention] and the small pro-etale site $C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use precisely the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings and constructed Tate lines of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]: $R_E=\mathcal O_{E,X}$, $K_E=E_X$, $A=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$,
$$
 L_E=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\left(\mu_{\ell^n,X}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_X}(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_X\right),\qquad
 Q_E=K_E\otimes_{R_E}L_E,\qquad
 Q_\Omega=\varinjlim_F Q_F.
$$
The integral limit has the coefficient-reduction and root-power transitions, and the last colimit is the sheafified colimit over the small directed poset of finite intermediate fields $F$ in $\Omega$, with its specified finite-extension transitions and $A$-action. In particular $A$ is the pullback of the finite-subextension-valued condensed coefficient ring. Read internal modules as sectionwise module sheaves through [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], and let restriction to $C/U$ mean [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

Then $L_E$, $Q_E$ and $Q_\Omega$ are finite locally free of constant rank one over $R_E$, $K_E$ and $A$, respectively. Here rank one means that on a covering of the terminal object each restricted module has a basis indexed by a singleton, equivalently is linearly isomorphic to its restricted coefficient ring. This asserts the three rank-one clauses for the signed twists at exponent $1$ of the constructed lines, whose exponent $0$ is the coefficient unit. No quasi-compactness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed on $X$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-route-sp-twists-common-cover] with this $X$, prime $\ell$ and fixed algebraic closure $\Omega$. Its hypotheses are exactly the residue-field invertibility and size hypotheses here. It supplies a pro-etale covering family $U_i\to X$. Clause 3, specialized to the chosen $E$, gives $R_E|_{U_i}$-linear isomorphisms $L_E|_{U_i}\cong R_E|_{U_i}$ and $K_E|_{U_i}$-linear isomorphisms $Q_E|_{U_i}\cong K_E|_{U_i}$. Clause 4 gives $A|_{U_i}$-linear isomorphisms $Q_\Omega|_{U_i}\cong A|_{U_i}$. These are the actual inverse-limit, scalar-extension and sheafified-colimit objects of this statement; in particular the algebraic-closure clause is over the pulled-back condensed ring, not a common-stage rational coefficient category. The cited lemma supplies all three on one family without a quasi-compactness hypothesis.

proof.text: Under [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], underlying sections and restrictions are unchanged, so the linear isomorphisms in step 1 are isomorphisms of the sectionwise module sheaves occurring in the recorded Lean conclusion. The signed-twist convention of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] at exponent $1$ is the one-fold tensor power of the line, canonically the line itself. With the recursive tensor-power convention starting at the unit, its unit constraint is explicitly $a\otimes m\mapsto am$, inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. These formulas commute with restrictions and are linear, so the same local trivializations apply to the signed exponent-$1$ objects; exponent $0$ is exactly the respective coefficient unit.

proof.text: For each of the three module sheaves $M$ with coefficient ring $R$, write $e_i:M|_{U_i}\cong R|_{U_i}$ for step 1's isomorphism (composed with step 2's unit constraint when required). On the localized site of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], set $s_i=e_i^{-1}(1)$. Linearity gives $e_i^{-1}(a)=a s_i$ for every local scalar $a$, so the singleton family $\{s_i\}$ is a basis: its free-module map $a\mapsto a s_i$ has inverse $e_i$. Thus this covering and these singleton generating families give the local generators data with generator index $\operatorname{Fin}(1)$ in the definition of finite locally free of rank one. This proves each of the three clauses and hence their conjunction. On the empty scheme the covering criterion is vacuous, as is that same definition.
